Plasma diffusion due to magnetic field fluctuations

has been studied in two dimensions for a plasma near

thermal equilibrium and when the fluctuations are supra-

thermal. I t i s found that near thermal equilibrium _2

electron diffusion varies as B when the collisionless

skin depth is greater than the thermal electron gyro-

radius and is generally smaller than the diffusion due

to collisions or electrostatic fluctuations for a low- 6

I. Introduction

Anomalous plasma diffusiop due to electric and magnetic

fluctuations in a confining magnetic field has been one of

the critical issues for the successful achievement for controlled

thermonuclear fusion. From the earliest days to the present,

confinement of plasmas has been the major subject along with

plasma heating in order to achieve the thermonuclear reaction.

It was Bohm who pointed out that the enhanced electric and magnetic

field fluctuations could give rise to -momalous diffusion which

could be orders of magnitude greater than the cljswi CCI 1 diffusion

in high temperature collisionless plasmas. While the high

temperature plasmas confined in a strong magnetic field are likely

subject to instabilities of various origin, it was hoped that the

plasma diffusion could follow the classical diffusion when the

instabilities are suppressed and the fluctuations are those of

thermal noise level.

It was recently pointed out that the problem of anomalous

plasma diffusion goes much deeper than it was believed in the 2

earlier days. As fusion plasma achieves higher and higher tem­

perature, it was shown that even the thermal fluctuations can

dominate over the classical diffusion for the transport of particles

and energy across the magnetic field. While the enhanced diffu­

sion due to thermal fluctuations may be greater than the clerical

diffusion, it is often too small to explain the experimental results

unless the fluctuation level is above the thermal noise. There are

mechanisms for plasma instabilities to feed the energy into thermal

fluctuations so that the diffusion is greatly enhanced.


<!-- Page 4 -->


-3-

Excitation of large amplitude connective cells due to drift

instabilities is one of such examples. However, these studies on

anomalous diffusion have been restricted primarily on electro­

static fluctuations appropriate only for low density and low

temperature plasmas.

Recently, it was pointed out that thermal magnetic field

fluctuations could give rije to enhanced diffusion comparable to 4 classical diffusion. It was shown, however, that diffusion is

generally smaller than the diffusion due to electrostatic fluctua- 5 tions near thermal equilibrium. In practice, there are many

situations where a plasma is c?rrying currents which then enhance

magnetic fluctuations. Under such cases, it is possible that the

diffusion caused by magnetic field fluctuation may dominate

over the diffusion due to electrostatic fluctuations. This is

particularly true for the electrons since they can diffuse much

faster along th° field lines than the ions owing to their

large thermal speed.

In this paper, we consider a two dimensional problem in

which a plasma is immersed in a strong external uniform magnetic

field, B , aligned along the 2 direction. We consider first the

case where the fluctuations are thermal. It is found that when

the electron-ion collisions are taken into account appropriately,

the electron diffusion arising from magnetic fluctuations varies — 2 as B when the collisionless skin depth is larger than the

electron gyroradius. This diffusion is generally smaller than

the classical diffusion and it is also smaller than the diffusion

due to the electrostatic fluctuation in a low-g plasma.


<!-- Page 5 -->


-4-

When there are macroscopic currents present, diffusion is

enhanced by magnetic fluctuations which can dominate the diffu­

sion caused by electrostatic fluctuations. Under such conditions

it was found that the current filaments and the magnetic field

fluctuations tend to coalesce into larger filaments and islands

owing to the nonlinear interactions among the current filaments.

The resultant rapid electron motion along the field lines further

enhance the coalescense and thermal electron diffusion. It was

found that the magnetic field energy condenses at the longest

wavelength mode available and stay there for the time scale longer

than that determined from the electron diffusion. This is because

the coalescense of islands takes place exclusively among the cur­

rent filaments in the same direction, and the current.,jK?.utraliza-

tion cannot take place on the same time scale even if the electrons

are apparently spread out more or less smoothly over the entire

region.

In the following, theoretical considerations on plasma diffu­

sion due to various origins are given in Sec. II. Simulation

results and the comparison with theory are given in Sec. Ill for

a thermal plasma. Enhanced magnetic fluctuations due to macro­

scopic current filaments and electron diffusion are studied in

Sec. IV. Discussion and concluding remarks are given in Sec. V.

IV. Suprathermal Magnetic Fluctuations

We have seen the diffusion of electrons due to magnetic

field fluctuations to be rather modest and is generally smaller

than the diffusion caused by electrostatic fluctuations when the

fluctuations are at the * .ermal level. There are situations,

however, where the magnetic field fluctuations are considerably

higher than the thermal nois^ level even when the electrostatic

flu'.cuations are not enhanced. This is because the laboratory

plasmas are often unstable with respect to magnetic field fluctua­

tions which could enhance the particle diffusion. Current carry­

ing plasmas can also enhance magnetic field fluctuations.

In this section, enhanced magnetic fluctuations and their

nonlinear interactions are considered along with the enhanced

V. Discussions and Conclusions

Particle diffusion due to magnetic field fluctuations in

two dimensions has been studied in some detail. When the fluctua­

tions are of thermal level, the diffusion varies as B in general

and is smaller than that caused by electrostatic fluctuations for

a low 3 plasma. When the macroscopic currents are present, mag­

netic field fluctuations can cause diffusion which exceeds the

diffusion due to electrostatic fluctuations. Coalescence of mag­

netic islands and current filaments results due to the nonlinear

interaction (mode co ig) of the current filaments and the

resultant streaming 01 filectrons along the field lines. The latter

is du;" 1 to the kinetic nature of a plasma. Large scale magnetic

islands persist longer than the time scale of particle diffusion.

It should be emphasized that the results presented here are

only two-dimensional while the real experiments are three dimensional.

It is true that the three-dimensional variations of magnetic field

lines are much more complicated and can be quite different. How­

ever, two-dimensional situation can also take place in three

dimensions. Our results show that the magnetic fluctuations tend

to develop into a coherent structure which would then compete with

the stochastic wandering of each individual field line which can

take place in three dimensions. Which process is more important?

This is not known and the detailed work is underway using a three-

dimensional simulation model.
